about.title: Gilroy Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Gilroy's traffic mix, from Leavesley Road and 1st Street to the US-101 corridor and Monterey Highway, sees real collision activity, and in the most recent full year, two of those crashes ended in a traffic fatality. Behind each of those numbers is a family in Gilroy trying to process a loss that arrived without warning. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim, and a limited group of other dependents may qualify if no closer relative exists. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. If someone you love died because of another person's negligence on a Gilroy road or elsewhere, reaching out costs nothing and starts a conversation, not a commitment.

items.title: Who Can File Matters
items.desc: California limits standing to certain people, typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents or heirs if no closer relative exists. We can clarify where your Gilroy family fits before any claim moves forward.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than People Expect
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and that window shrinks significantly if a government entity, like a public roadway agency, is involved. Waiting to gather documents can quietly cost a family its right to file.

items.title: Civil and Criminal Cases Run Separately
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil matter distinct from any criminal charges tied to the crash. Families in Gilroy don't need to wait for a criminal case to resolve, or even for charges to be filed, before exploring a civil claim.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on a road like Monterey Highway or US-101 through Gilroy?
items.answer: The specific road matters less than who was at fault and what evidence exists, but corridor-specific collision patterns can sometimes help us understand contributing factors. Public crash-record data for roads like Leavesley Road or 1st Street may also be relevant depending on the case. We can review the details free of charge.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally two years from the date of death, though that deadline is shorter if a government entity is a potential defendant. Missing this window can permanently bar a claim, so it's worth having the timeline reviewed early. We can walk through the specifics with you.
